title: Collisions: momentum balances, energy leaks
objective: Learners watch one cart hit another on a frictionless track and see that total momentum is exactly the same before and after in every case, that kinetic energy is the same only when the collision is elastic, and that the mass ratio decides who bounces back, who keeps going and who stops dead.

recommended.why: The carts, their velocity arrows and the momentum and energy bars moving in real time make the two conservation laws visible as a picture, not a pair of equations.

alternative.why: The animation shows the event; the velocity-time chart shows the before and after as flat lines with one step, with momentum and energy totals underneath. Which one convinces a sceptic that momentum did not change?

assumptions: One-dimensional collision on a frictionless track; cart 1 has a mass of 1 kg and cart 2 the chosen multiple of it; cart 2 starts at rest
The coefficient of restitution (elasticity) sets the velocities after the hit: 1 is perfectly elastic, 0 means the carts stick
Momentum is conserved exactly; the kinetic energy lost is ½ μ (1 − e²) (v₁ − v₂)² with μ the reduced mass
Cart lengths grow with mass so the picture reads; the collision happens when the gap between them closes
Playback runs in real time for 8 s
checkDescription: Momentum after equals momentum before exactly; kinetic energy is unchanged when elastic and lower otherwise, with the loss matching the closed form; sticking gives one shared velocity; equal masses and elastic swap velocities; the carts never pass through each other and the series keeps the momentum total at every sample.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the mass ratio to 4 before you play. Does cart 1 keep going, stop, or bounce back, and how fast does cart 2 move off?
learnerPrompts.explain: With elasticity 0 the carts stick and energy is lost, yet momentum is unchanged. Where did the energy go, and why can momentum not go there too?
